sensor: airborne lidar transect plots, Landsat time series
validation_design: lidar plots as calibration and validation
notes: The national Canadian structure product a British Columbia design would sit against.

title: Fire, fragmentation, and windstorms: A recipe for tropical forest degradation
method: pre and post-windstorm field mortality with airborne lidar tree heights and canopy gap metrics across a replicated burn experiment
agent: windstorm, fire, and edge effects, interacting
host: southeastern Amazonian forest, three 50 ha plots
support: plot, individual tree over 10 cm DBH
validation_design: replicated fire experiment with control and two burn frequencies
accuracy_metric: mortality rate and mode of death
accuracy_value: greater windstorm damage in burned plots than control, exact figures not extracted from abstract
notes: Rare experimental test of interaction between two disturbance agents on the same forest. Agents are wind and fire, both abiotic.

title: Quantifying long-term changes in carbon stocks and forest structure from Amazon forest degradation
method: annual Landsat time series combined with high-density airborne lidar to quantify carbon and structural change by degradation type
accuracy_value: degraded forests contained 45.1% of the carbon stocks of intact forests, with differences persisting after 15 years of regrowth
notes: Compares logging against fire as degradation pathways with different structural consequences.

title: Measuring short-term post-fire forest recovery across a burn severity gradient in a mixed pine-oak forest using multi-sensor remote sensing techniques
method: 1 m simultaneous airborne imaging spectroscopy and lidar with 2 m satellite imagery to separate canopy from understory recovery
sensor: airborne imaging spectroscopy and lidar at 1 m, satellite multispectral at 2 m
agent: wildfire, across a burn severity gradient
notes: Uses structure specifically to remove understory contamination from a spectral recovery signal, a confound that also afflicts open fir stands.

title: Urban tree health assessment using airborne hyperspectral and LiDAR imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: lidar-based tree detection and segmentation then PLSR models of chlorophyll and leaf area index from canopy spectra, with structural metrics
agent: declining tree health, agent not identified
accuracy_metric: segmentation accuracy, RMSE and R squared
accuracy_value: tree delineation average accuracy 91%; chlorophyll RMSE 2.8 micrograms per cm2 R2 0.77; LAI RMSE 0.5 R2 0.66
notes: Well-reported fusion workflow with explicit accuracies at each step.

title: The extent of mangrove change and potential for recovery following severe Tropical Cyclone Yasi, Hinchinbrook Island, Queensland, Australia
method: foliage projective cover from Landsat with aerial and RapidEye imagery to map severe windthrow and recovery
notes: Damage varied by dominant species and structure, which is a host-effect confound of the type this design removes.

title: Detection of windthrows and insect outbreaks by L-band SAR: A case study in the Bavarian Forest National Park
method: change detection on L-band spaceborne SAR backscatter, applied separately to wind-damaged and insect-damaged areas
host: Bavarian Forest National Park, Norway spruce dominated
validation_design: not stated in abstract; accuracy ranges given by acquisition date and environmental condition
accuracy_value: wind damage 69 to 84%; insect outbreaks 65 to 88%; susceptible or initial green-attack areas 64 to 74%
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ3, already cited as Tanase 2018. Two agents in one park on one dominant host, but the abstract reports delineation of each agent's areas separately rather than a classifier that decides between them, and one agent is abiotic. It is the closest published approach to the target design and its green-attack accuracy of 64 to 74% is the realistic ceiling for early insect detection from radar.

title: Mapping canopy defoliation by herbivorous insects at the individual tree level using bi-temporal airborne imaging spectroscopy and LiDAR measurements
method: bi-temporal airborne imaging spectroscopy and lidar at 1 m, ordinary least squares models fitted from each sensor alone and combined
host: mixed oak-pine forest, Long Island, New York
validation_design: bi-temporal, model comparison; split design not stated in abstract
accuracy_metric: adjusted R squared and RMSE for defoliation severity
accuracy_value: lidar only adj. R2 0.77 RMSE 15.37%; imaging spectroscopy only adj. R2 0.63 RMSE 19.11%; combined adj. R2 0.81 RMSE 14.46%
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ3. The lidar-only model outperformed the hyperspectral-only model for mapping insect defoliation at individual tree level, and the combination beat both. This establishes that structure carries insect damage information at least as well as spectra, so that part of the project's hypothesis is supported rather than novel. Named lidar metrics were B70, intensity skewness and kurtosis.

title: Characterizing Tropical Forest Cover Loss Using Dense Sentinel-1 Data and Active Fire Alerts
method: near real-time radar forest cover loss combined with active fire alerts, separating fires that predate, coincide with and postdate loss
sensor: Sentinel-1 C-band SAR, VIIRS active fire alerts
agent: fire versus other causes of forest cover loss
host: natural and plantation forest, Riau, Indonesia
support: medium spatial scale, high temporal detail
notes: Attribution of loss to fire by relative timing rather than by signal shape. A useful precedent for using an independent agent-specific data stream as the attribution key.

title: Ensemble classification of individual Pinus crowns from multispectral satellite imagery and airborne LiDAR
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: ensemble classification of individual crowns under three schemes: lidar alone, WorldView-2 alone, and both combined
sensor: high-density airborne lidar at 160 returns per m2, WorldView-2
host: Pinus sylvestris and Pinus uncinata, Barcelonnette
notes: Closest available test of whether crown structure separates two congeneric conifers. Relevant because this project must hold host constant and needs to know how much structure varies by species alone.

title: Impacts of Water Stress on Forest Recovery and Its Interaction with Canopy Height
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
method: regional analysis of post-drought recovery paths stratified by lidar-derived canopy height and water availability
sensor: lidar-derived canopy height, satellite vegetation records
notes: Canopy height modifies the recovery signal after an agent, so structure is a covariate of damage response as well as a predictor of it.

title: Fusion of NASA Airborne Snow Observatory (ASO) Lidar Time Series over Mountain Forest Landscapes
method: coherent merging of weekly snow-survey lidar acquisitions to build a dense multi-year point cloud time series
agent: fire, insect damage and drought, named as targets
accuracy_value: weekly acquisitions at about 1 point per m2 merged to about 12 points per m2
notes: Shows how repeat lidar can be assembled opportunistically from acquisitions flown for another purpose, which is the situation with provincial lidar coverage.

title: Classification for non infected and infected ganoderma boninense of oil palm trees using ALOS PALSAR-2 backscattering coefficient
venue: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environment
method: decision tree classification of infected versus non-infected trees from HH and HV backscatter
notes: Radar backscatter alone used to classify infection status of a single host. Plantation, and the disease attacks the stem base rather than the canopy.

title: Assessing the Trade-Offs of SPOT7 Imagery for Monitoring Natural Forest Canopy Intactness
method: comparison of canopy gap detection accuracy between two pan-sharpening resolutions, with NDVI and SAR tested as accuracy enhancers
sensor: SPOT7 at 5 m and 1.5 m, SAR
notes: Tests whether adding radar improves an optical gap product.

title: Current remote sensing approaches to monitoring forest degradation in support of countries measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) systems for REDD+
method: review of degradation monitoring approaches, split between canopy cover change detection and biomass loss quantification
notes: States that no single method can monitor degradation because the answer depends on the degradation type and the observation window.

title: Remote sensing of forest insect disturbances: Current state and future directions
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: systematic review grouping studies into bark beetles, broadleaved defoliators and coniferous defoliators, comparing sensors and methods within and across types
notes: CENTRAL RECORD. Senf et al. 2017. Its first stated future research direction is verbatim 'Separate insect disturbances from other agents', which is an explicit statement that the separation problem was open at that date. It also finds substantial differences between methods used for mapping bark beetles and defoliators. Not in references.bib.

title: Monitoring of Forest Structure Dynamics by Means of L-Band SAR Tomography
method: compressive sensing tomographic reconstruction of 3D reflectivity profiles, with horizontal and vertical structure indices from local maxima
sensor: L-band tomographic SAR, simulated and experimental
notes: Radar tomography producing explicit horizontal and vertical structure indices, the closest radar analogue to lidar structural metrics.

title: Using Intra-Annual Landsat Time Series for Attributing Forest Disturbance Agents in Central Europe
method: breakpoint detection on all available Landsat observations 1984 to 2016, then classification of four disturbance classes from spectral, temporal and topographic metrics
agent: windthrow, cleared windthrow, bark beetles, other harvest
host: Central European forest, three sites, managed and protected
validation_design: three sites, design not further stated in abstract
notes: Seed study, cited as Oeser 2017. Two of the four classes are the same agent in different management states. The abstract states verbatim that temporal proximity to storm events was among the most important predictors and that elevation information was very effective for discriminating disturbance agents, so a substantial part of the discrimination comes from site and timing rather than from the damage signature itself.

title: Individual Tree Crown Delineation from Airborne Laser Scanning for Diseased Larch Forest Stands
method: comparison of marker-controlled watershed and region growing crown segmentation across infection levels
sensor: airborne laser scanning canopy height models
validation_design: sample plots at two sites across a range of infection levels
notes: Shows that disease-induced canopy irregularity degrades the crown segmentation that a tree-level structural analysis depends on. A methodological warning for this project.

title: Prediction of Forest Canopy and Surface Fuels from Lidar and Satellite Time Series Data in a Bark Beetle-Affected Forest
method: random forest predicting field-measured canopy and surface fuels from lidar and Landsat time series, with correlation against mortality severity
agent: mountain pine beetle (Dendroctonus ponderosae), six years post-outbreak
accuracy_value: 59% available canopy fuel, 48% canopy bulk density, 35% canopy base height, 70% for the fourth attribute
notes: Quantifies how much structural variation lidar plus optical explains six years after an insect outbreak, which is a realistic expectation for a lagged structural signal.

title: Episodic Canopy Structural Transformations and Biological Invasion in a Hawaiian Forest
method: multi-temporal high-resolution lidar quantifying near-decadal net change in canopy height and gap distribution
agent: drought, host-specific insect outbreak (Scotorythra paludicola), invasive species
host: Hawaiian sub-montane native forest, Mauna Kea
accuracy_value: net loss in average canopy height, exact value not extracted from abstract
notes: Three interacting drivers including a host-specific insect, observed structurally. The drivers are described together, not separated.

title: Measuring leaf water content using multispectral terrestrial laser scanning
method: multispectral terrestrial laser scanning intensity ratios regressed on measured leaf water content
sensor: multispectral terrestrial laser scanning at 690, 905 and 1550 nm
agent: tree stress preceding drought, insect and pathogen damage
accuracy_value: a ratio of 905 nm and 1550 nm explained 84% of variation in leaf water content, prediction accuracy 0.0041 g per cm2
notes: Establishes the physical mechanism behind dual-wavelength lidar stress detection under controlled conditions.

title: Remote sensing of seasonal changes and disturbances in mangrove forest: a case study from South Florida
method: four vegetation indices from 150 Landsat scenes with lidar, separating seasonal variation from episodic disturbance
accuracy_value: normalized difference moisture index performed best; chilling and hurricane damage showed distinct spatial patterns
notes: Two abiotic agents on one forest type distinguished by spatial pattern rather than by spectral signature, and separated from a seasonal cycle. The spatial-pattern route is a viable alternative to a signature-based route.

title: Forest Disturbances and Regrowth Assessment Using ALOS PALSAR Data from 2007 to 2010 in Vietnam, Cambodia and Lao PDR
method: expectation maximisation change detection on L-band SAR mosaics for disturbance and regrowth
host: tropical forest, Vietnam, Cambodia, Lao PDR
validation_design: training and testing database, described as reliable
notes: L-band chosen because intensity is sensitive to biomass loss, the opposite trade-off from C-band foliage sensitivity.

title: Post-Fire Changes in Forest Biomass Retrieved by Airborne LiDAR in Amazonia
method: airborne lidar quantification of post-fire canopy height and biomass change with 25 inventory plots
notes: Fire histories five years apart give a structural recovery gradient from a single agent.

title: The Impact of Fine-Scale Disturbances on the Predictability of Vegetation Dynamics and Carbon Flux
method: repeat lidar used to test the effect of fine-scale disturbance on the predictability of vegetation dynamics and carbon flux
agent: fine-scale disturbance, plus cyclones, fire and pest outbreaks as contrast
notes: Argues that small frequent disturbances may matter as much as large extreme events, which is the severity regime of the adelgid record.

title: Remote Sensing of Tamarisk Biomass, Insect Herbivory, and Defoliation: Novel Methods in the Grand Canyon Region, Arizona
method: classification of host distribution and beetle defoliation from 0.2 m airborne multispectral, with lidar biomass estimation
sensor: airborne multispectral at 0.2 m, airborne lidar at 100 points per m2
agent: northern tamarisk beetle (Diorhabda carinulata), a deliberately introduced biocontrol agent
accuracy_value: 86 percent; mean leaf biomass loss 0.52 kg per m2, 25,692 kg across the study area
notes: Combines a spectral defoliation map with a lidar biomass model to convert defoliation into mass loss.

title: Development of monitoring methods for Hemlock Woolly Adelgid induced tree mortality within a Southern Appalachian landscape with inhibited access
method: semi-automatic mapping of conifer patches including living hemlock and adelgid-caused mortality from aerial data
sensor: aerial imagery, further sensors not stated in abstract
host: eastern hemlock (Tsuga canadensis) and Carolina hemlock (Tsuga caroliniana)
notes: Directly relevant to RQ1. Emphasises that the landscape carries several other conifer species, so the host must be isolated before the agent can be mapped, the same sequencing this project requires.

title: Mapping dynamics of deforestation and forest degradation in tropical forests using radar satellite data
method: detection algorithm on L-band backscatter allowing repeated disturbance on the same land and separating slow from fast recovery
agent: deforestation, degradation from selective logging, successional dynamics
host: tropical forest, Madre de Dios, Peru
accuracy_metric: area disturbed and false positive rate
accuracy_value: 2.3% of land disturbed over three years with a false positive rate of 0.3% of area; low but significant detection rate for sparse small-scale selective logging
notes: One of the few radar studies that reports a false positive rate as area, which is the honest way to report a rare-class detector.

title: Discriminating disturbance from natural variation with LiDAR in semi-arid forests in the southwestern USA
method: local indicators of spatial association applied to airborne lidar tree structure to separate disturbance from background variation
agent: previously recorded but poorly defined forest disturbances
notes: Addresses the prior question this project must answer first, whether a structural anomaly is a disturbance at all before asking which agent caused it.

title: Spatial Wavelet Statistics of SAR Backscatter for Characterizing Degraded Forest: A Case Study From Cameroon
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
method: supervised analysis of SAR backscatter spatial statistics via wavelet frames, wavelet variance scaling signatures
validation_design: supervised classification of intact versus degraded forest
notes: Radar texture rather than radar amplitude as the structural descriptor. A route to structure from radar that does not need tomography or interferometry.

title: Estimation of Vertical Structure of Forests fromMultibaseline SAR data: A Performance Analysis
method: performance analysis of multibaseline SAR tomography for estimating vertical forest structure
agent: disturbance regime, as a motivating application
notes: Names disturbance regime assessment as a target of radar vertical structure retrieval.

title: Classification of Plot-Level Fire-Caused Tree Mortality in a Redwood Forest Using Digital Orthophotography and LiDAR
method: classification of plot percent mortality from colour-infrared imagery with post-fire lidar and with differenced pre and post-fire lidar
host: second-growth coast redwood, Santa Cruz California
class_balance_reported: yes, mortality categorised into ordered classes
accuracy_metric: classification accuracy of plot mortality class
notes: Directly compares imagery alone, imagery plus single-date lidar, and imagery plus differenced lidar. The ablation design this project needs.

title: Early Detection of Bark Beetle Green Attack Using TerraSAR-X and RapidEye Data
method: three statistical approaches applied to radar and optical data separately and combined to separate healthy from green-attack areas
notes: One of the earliest tests of high-resolution X-band radar for the hardest insect detection case, green attack, with optical as a comparator.

title: Area-Based Mapping of Defoliation of Scots Pine Stands Using Airborne Scanning LiDAR
method: lidar canopy mask then plot-level defoliation prediction from above-mask returns
sensor: airborne scanning lidar, plot training data
notes: Area-based lidar defoliation mapping for one insect, integrable with standard area-based forest inventory.

title: Classification of Needle Loss of Individual Scots Pine Trees by Means of Airborne Laser Scanning
method: classification of individual tree needle loss from airborne laser scanning features
notes: Tree-level structural classification of insect needle loss.

title: Landscape-scale analysis of aboveground tree carbon stocks affected by mountain pine beetles in Idaho
method: multispectral classification of green, red and grey attack stages with lidar-based aboveground carbon models
sensor: multispectral imagery, airborne lidar, field observations
accuracy_value: 39% of the forested area killed by beetles; 40 to 50% of aboveground carbon in beetle-killed trees
notes: Lidar supplies carbon, spectra supply attack stage. The two sensors do different jobs rather than competing.

title: Detecting trends in forest disturbance and recovery using yearly Landsat time series: 1. LandTrendr — Temporal segmentation algorithms
method: temporal segmentation of yearly Landsat time series stacks to extract disturbance and recovery trajectories
validation_design: described in the companion TimeSync paper
accuracy_metric: not stated in the resolved record
accuracy_value: not stated in the resolved record
notes: Kennedy et al. 2010, 1762 citations in this dataset. The base algorithm on which most subsequent optical agent-attribution work rests, including Oeser 2017 and Morin-Bernard 2023. Absent from references.bib. Only the Semantic Scholar TLDR was retrieved, not the publisher abstract, so no verbatim quotation from the paper is offered here.

title: Detecting trends in forest disturbance and recovery using yearly Landsat time series: 2. TimeSync — Tools for calibration and validation
method: human interpretation tool for calibrating and validating Landsat time series segmentation against plot chronologies
sensor: Landsat time series with high-resolution imagery for interpretation
accuracy_metric: not stated in the resolved record
accuracy_value: not stated in the resolved record
notes: Cohen et al. 2010. The reference-data protocol that most optical attribution studies use for validation, and a template for how this project should build its reference set. Absent from references.bib.

title: Classification of Defoliated Trees Using Tree-Level Airborne Laser Scanning Data Combined with Aerial Images
method: logistic LASSO regression, random forest and most similar neighbour predicting individual tree defoliation level from ALS features and aerial image features, singly and combined
accuracy_value: 83.7% (kappa 0.67) to 88.1% (kappa 0.76) depending on method; the most accurate result came from random forest with both sensors combined
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ3. Tree-level insect defoliation classified from structure plus imagery, with the combined model beating either sensor alone. The sensor-ablation result this project's H1 predicts, already published for one agent.

title: Integration of LIDAR and Digital Aerial Imagery for Detailed Estimates of Lodgepole Pine (Pinus contorta) Volume Killed by Mountain Pine Beetle (Dendroctonus ponderosae)
method: sample-based plot estimation combining lidar dominant heights with photo-interpreted attack status on 55 photo-plots
notes: The closest prior work geographically. British Columbia, lidar plus imagery, insect-killed volume at plot support, using attack stage from photo interpretation. Establishes that the lidar-plus-imagery route has been taken in this province for a different insect.

title: Forest disturbance and recovery: A general review in the context of spaceborne remote sensing of impacts on aboveground biomass and canopy structure
method: general review of spaceborne remote sensing of disturbance impacts on aboveground biomass and canopy structure
sensor: passive optical and near-infrared, high-resolution imagery, small-footprint lidar (review)
agent: fire, windstorms, logging, shifting cultivation, land conversion, flooding, landslides, avalanches
accuracy_value: abrupt disturbances generating gaps over 0.001 km2 affect roughly 0.4 to 0.7 million km2 per year
notes: Frolking et al. 2009. Notes that high-resolution and small-footprint lidar can map crown geometry and gaps but has rarely been applied at the scale needed, which is still true for agent attribution.

title: Airborne Laser Scanning Quantification of Disturbances from Hurricanes and Lightning Strikes to Mangrove Forests in Everglades National Park, USA
method: pre and post-event airborne lidar comparison of canopy height distribution and gap counts at two sites
sensor: airborne lidar before and after the 2005 hurricane season
agent: hurricanes (Katrina and Wilma) and lightning strikes
validation_design: paired pre and post-event acquisitions at two sites
accuracy_metric: change in canopy proportion and gap density
accuracy_value: gaps per square kilometre increased from about 400 to 500 up to 4000 after the hurricanes
notes: Two biotic-free agents of different spatial grain, hurricanes and lightning strikes, distinguished structurally within one forest. Lightning gaps are small and isolated, hurricane damage is diffuse, so the separation rests on spatial pattern rather than on the damage signature.

title: Evaluating the consistency of forest disturbance datasets in continental USA
method: cross-comparison of five disturbance datasets for spatial extent, timing and causal agent
agent: multiple, as labelled by each product
notes: Directly relevant to label quality. Compares causal agent assignment across products where available, which is the closest published check on how much agent labels disagree.

title: Deep Learning for Satellite‐Based Forest Disturbance Monitoring: Recent Advances and Challenges
venue: WIREs Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
method: review of deep learning for satellite-based disturbance detection, mapping and attribution
notes: Describes classifying disturbances into different agents as the complex end of the task spectrum, above mapping logging or burned area.

title: Assessing Drought-Induced Tree Mortality in Open Mediterranean Forests Integrating Landsat Time Series, Spectral Unmixing, and UAS Validation
method: LandTrendr applied to NDVI, NDWI and spectral unmixing vegetation cover, validated against UAS imagery
validation_design: UAS imagery validated against field data
notes: Open canopies and mixed pixels named as the core obstacle, the same geometry as open fir stands.

title: Identifying the Impact of Leaf-Miner Complex Insects on Nothofagus obliqua Forests by Assessing Changes in Land Surface Phenology
method: seasonal-trend decomposition of MODIS EVI 2003 to 2024 with an EVI condition index against a historical baseline
agent: leaf-miner complex dominated by Heterobathmia pseuderiocrania
notes: Names signal attribution as the explicit problem: attributing phenological anomalies to biotic disturbance rather than to climate.

title: Spectral Responses to Larval and Artificial Defoliation in Eucalyptus dunnii: Implications for UAV-Based Detection of Gonipterus Damage
method: randomised complete block experiment with five replicates and four treatments, UAV 10-band multispectral over 16 days
agent: Gonipterus sp. n. 2 larval feeding versus artificial defoliation
validation_design: randomised complete block, five replicates, controlled inoculation levels
class_balance_reported: yes, four treatments with five replicates each
accuracy_value: reduction in visible and near-infrared reflectance in both larval and artificial treatments
notes: CENTRAL FOR THE ATTRIBUTION PROBLEM. Explicitly contrasts insect-caused defoliation with mechanically imposed defoliation of the same magnitude on the same host, which is the cleanest available test of whether a spectral signature is agent-specific or merely damage-specific. The abstract states verbatim that distinguishing insect-specific damage from general canopy stress remains challenging due to overlapping spectral signatures.

title: Unravelling the spatial and temporal variability of natural disturbances in European forests
method: Gaussian finite mixture models characterising disturbance regimes by causal agent from size, severity and frequency
sensor: Landsat-derived disturbance dataset, over 3.8 million events 1985 to 2023
host: European forest across boreal, temperate and Mediterranean biomes
notes: Shows that the three agents differ systematically in patch size, severity and frequency, which is why size and pattern predictors carry agent information in existing studies.

title: Discrimination of Bark Beetle-Damaged Forest Stands Using Vegetation Indices Derived from Landsat 8
method: statistical discrimination test of five vegetation indices between damaged and undamaged stands
host: coniferous stands, Arac Forest Directorate, Kastamonu
notes: One of the few records in the set with a deliberately balanced two-class design at stand support.

title: A Two-Step Framework for Mapping, Classification, and Area Estimation of Stand- and Non-Stand-Replacing Forest Disturbances
method: two-step framework, binary change detection with the Three Indices Three Dimensions algorithm then classification of disturbance type, with design-based area estimation
validation_design: area estimation suitable for national statistics
notes: Separates change detection from agent classification into two explicit steps, which is a defensible structure for this project's pipeline.

title: Global drivers of forest loss at 1 km resolution
method: classification of dominant driver of forest loss into seven classes at 1 km from satellite and ancillary data
sensor: Landsat, Sentinel, biophysical and population data
agent: seven drivers including permanent agriculture, wildfire and logging
notes: Global driver attribution at coarse support. None of the seven classes is an insect.

title: The European Forest Disturbance Atlas: a forest disturbance monitoring system using the Landsat archive
method: classification-based annual disturbance detection on a Landsat data cube, with layers for occurrence, severity and agent
agent: agent layer included, classes not enumerated in abstract
validation_design: compiled reference data on forest land use and disturbances
accuracy_value: total forest disturbed area of 439,000 km2 over 1985 to 2023
notes: The current continental-scale product carrying an agent attribute. Sets the operational baseline any new attribution claim is measured against.

title: Evaluation of Temporal Trends in Forest Health Status Using Precise Remote Sensing
method: YOLO deep learning object detection on UAV RGB imagery over four years
notes: Fir host and bark beetle agent, the same pairing as the western balsam bark beetle class in this project.

title: Post-fire delayed tree mortality in mesic coniferous forests reduces fire refugia and seed sources
method: annual mapping of live tree cover from 3 m satellite imagery up to three years post-fire
agent: high-severity wildfire and subsequent delayed mortality
host: mesic coniferous forest, Oregon western Cascades
accuracy_value: delayed mortality decreased live forest cover by 8.5% between one month and three years post-fire
notes: Quantifies the lag between an agent acting and the damage becoming visible, which is the timing problem in matching survey year to imagery year.

title: Assessment of regional scale-based bark beetle disturbance predisposition in complex terrain with earth observations
venue: Forestry: An International Journal of Forest Research
method: earth observation predictors of stand predisposition to infestation at 30 m in complex terrain
sensor: satellite earth observation, sensors not enumerated in abstract
agent: bark beetle, with wind as the co-dominant agent
notes: Predisposition rather than damage, and it names wind and bark beetle as the two dominant agents in the same landscape.

title: Detection of Larch Caterpillar Infestation in Typical Forest Areas of Changbai Mountain, China, Based on Integrated Satellite Hyperspectral and Multispectral Data
method: genetic algorithm feature selection over spectral indices, texture and fraction features from fused hyperspectral and multispectral imagery
notes: Argues that single data sources give insufficient spectral information for accurate insect detection.

title: Patterns and drivers of biotic disturbance hotspots in western United States coniferous forests
method: Bayesian spatio-temporal models of the occurrence of areas where two or more biotic agents co-occur
sensor: aerial survey based biotic disturbance records, 2000 to 2020
agent: multiple herbivorous insects and plant pathogens, co-occurring
host: coniferous forest, Southern Rockies, Middle Rockies and Cascades
notes: CENTRAL FOR THE CO-OCCURRENCE PROBLEM. Establishes that two or more biotic agents overlapping in space and time is a documented phenomenon in exactly the aerial survey records this project uses, and names it a biotic disturbance hotspot. It models where hotspots occur; it does not separate the agents from imagery.

title: Where is the Eastern Larch Beetle? An Exploration of Different Detection Methods in Northern Wisconsin
method: field survey of 50 stands or aerial detection polygons, comparing aerial sketch map polygons, a satellite algorithm and field observation
sensor: aerial sketch map survey, Astrape satellite algorithm, field survey
validation_design: field verification of 20 aerial survey polygons and 20 satellite-flagged stands
class_balance_reported: yes, 20 and 20 plus a third group stated
accuracy_metric: agreement between detection methods and field observation
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ4. Field-verifies aerial sketch map polygons against ground truth for a specific insect on a specific host, which is precisely the label-accuracy question this project's ceiling depends on.

title: FID-Net: A Feature-Enhanced Deep Learning Network for Forest Infestation Detection
method: YOLOv8n-based detector with feature enhancement and multi-scale fusion modules on UAV visible-light imagery
agent: forest pests, not named in abstract
notes: Preprint. Detection plus spatial pattern metrics.

title: Application of the meanshift segmentation method for tree crown delineation from UAV imagery using Orfeo ToolBox
method: MeanShift segmentation of crowns into three sanitary condition categories
notes: Fir host and bark beetle agent with condition classes matching the survey severity vocabulary.

title: Climate-linked cascading disturbances drive conifer forest decline in a boreal–temperate ecotone: evidence from Kunashir Island (Northwest Pacific)
venue: Forestry: An International Journal of Forest Research
method: convolutional neural networks on very high resolution satellite imagery to map windthrow then subsequent beetle outbreak
agent: extratropical cyclone followed by Japanese spruce bark beetle
host: Abies sachalinensis, Picea jezoensis, Picea glehnii, Kunashir Island
accuracy_value: windthrow patches covered 21.73 km2, 1.83% of island forest area, 97% in dark coniferous and mixed forests
notes: Two agents in sequence on the same conifer hosts, separated by timing and by the causal chain rather than by a classifier.

title: Has the tortoise scale exacerbated fire severity in Mediterranean stone pine forests?
method: fire behaviour simulation coupled with Landsat reflectance sensitivity analysis to insect abundance
agent: Toumeyella parvicornis (tortoise scale) interacting with wildfire
validation_design: two experimental designs, described in the abstract
accuracy_metric: band sensitivity and fire type proportions
accuracy_value: only NIR, green and SWIR 2 were sensitive to T. parvicornis abundance; 62.7% surface fires in unthinned stands versus 37.3% conditional fire types
notes: An insect agent modifying the severity of a second agent, which is a different kind of interaction from co-occurrence.

title: Changes in planned and unplanned canopy openings are linked in Europe’s forests
method: attribution of the root cause of all stand-replacing canopy disturbances identified from Landsat, split into planned and unplanned
agent: human land use versus wind, bark beetles and wildfire
accuracy_metric: share of disturbed area by cause
accuracy_value: human canopy openings account for 82% of the area disturbed; planned openings increased 24% and unplanned 30% relative to the late twentieth century
notes: Continental attribution, but the binary is human versus natural, with wind, beetle and fire grouped together as unplanned.

title: Large-scale remote sensing reveals that tree mortality in Germany appears to be greater than previously expected
method: random forest regression of standing deadwood maps at 10 m on biotic and abiotic environmental drivers, with drone-image reference
sensor: Sentinel 10 m maps of standing deadwood, drone imagery as reference
agent: biotic and abiotic drivers, analysed jointly
validation_design: hundreds of drone images as the reference for mortality
notes: Preprint. Drone imagery as a scalable reference source, an alternative to the aerial survey polygons this project relies on.

title: deadtrees.earth - An Open-Access and Interactive Database for Centimeter-Scale Aerial Imagery to Uncover Global Tree Mortality Dynamics
method: open database of centimetre-resolution drone orthophotos of tree mortality for training supervised models
sensor: drone orthophotos at sub-centimetre to centimetre resolution
accuracy_value: more than a thousand orthophotos covering more than 300,000 units as stated
notes: Preprint. A reference-data resource that could supply independent validation for mortality but not for agent identity.

title: A Deep Semantic Segmentation Approach to Map Forest Tree Dieback in Sentinel-2 Data
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
method: U-Net semantic segmentation with attention and self-distillation on Sentinel-2
agent: insect outbreaks, pests, fires and windstorms named collectively
notes: Dieback segmentation with agents named but not separated.

title: Combining Sentinel-2 Data and Risk Maps to Detect Trees Predisposed to and Attacked by European Spruce Bark Beetle
method: random forest on Sentinel-2 pixels combined with a geodata and forestry risk map, fitted per date across two seasons
host: Norway spruce, southern Sweden, two 90 by 90 km tiles
validation_design: per-date models across May to September in 2017 and 2018
accuracy_metric: detection accuracy as a function of time since swarming
notes: Combines a susceptibility prior with a spectral detector, which is the same structure as combining abiotic covariates with spectra in Campbell et al. 2023.

title: Early Detection of Dendroctonus valens Infestation with UAV-Based Thermal and Hyperspectral Images
method: random forest on four spectral datasets and one temperature dataset to classify three tree states
accuracy_value: differences between healthy and early-infested trees occur mainly in the near-infrared
notes: Three states, healthy, early-infested and dead, from spectra plus canopy temperature.

title: Leveraging Sentinel-2 time series for bark beetle-induced forest dieback inventory
method: random forest, XGBoost and U-Net compared on Sentinel-2 bands and indices, with and without temporal information
notes: Isolates the contribution of temporal information to detection performance.

title: Towards scalable wide area UAS monitoring of forest disturbance using hydrogen powered airships
method: beyond visual line of sight hydrogen-powered airship UAS monitoring flights in three seasons
sensor: airship-borne UAS sensors, not enumerated in abstract
agent: bark beetles and other disturbance agents
notes: Platform paper. Relevant only to acquisition logistics.

title: Bark beetle detection method using electronic nose sensors. A possible improvement of early forest disturbance detection?
venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
method: electronic nose sensors detecting volatile compounds with microclimate signs in stands
sensor: electronic nose gas sensors, in-stand rather than remote
notes: Included because of its verbatim statement of the limit of spectral detection: in some cases, the attacked trees do not change their appearance, and based on calculations of vegetation indices from remote sensing data, the attack cannot be mapped. Not a remote sensing method.

title: Identification of drought-induced forest damage in 2022 and of its key site condition drivers through satellite imagery
method: image classification of a drought year against a reference year without drought
accuracy_metric: proportion of stands by damage class
accuracy_value: stands with defoliation over 50% doubled to 19.3%, 417,000 ha; 223,000 ha increased defoliation by 30% or more
notes: Uses a clean reference year rather than a within-year control, an approach available where a pre-outbreak epoch exists.

title: Characterization of Change in Tree Cover State and Condition over the Conterminous United States
method: annual land cover and change time series with map validation reference plots to characterise tree cover change processes
agent: disturbance and extreme climate events, processes not individually named
notes: Operational product with a documented reference-plot validation design.

title: Land Surface Phenology Reveals Region-Specific Hurricane Impacts Across the North Atlantic Basin (2001–2022)
method: pre and post-hurricane land surface phenology from EVI for 44 hurricanes over 22 years, storms grouped by climate attributes
host: North Atlantic Basin forest, six subregions
validation_design: comparison across six subregions and wind speed classes
accuracy_value: Southeast US showed EVI decline in the first winter and first year; four other regions showed no increased impact with wind speed
notes: A negative result on transferability: the same agent produces a detectable phenological signal in some regions and none in others.

title: Automated attribution of forest disturbance types from remote sensing data: A synthesis
method: systematic synthesis of 34 studies that automated the attribution of two or more forest disturbance types, with metrics on context, method and outcome
agent: eight disturbance categories: harvest, land-use change, wildfire, context-specific change, biotic disturbances or other stress, infrastructure, weather, hydrologic processes
support: pixel, approximated as 900 m2 Landsat or 1 km2 MODIS
validation_design: 30 of 34 studies reported overall accuracy; evaluation data were on-screen interpretation, field data, or inventory and disturbance datasets
accuracy_value: about 80% for up to eight disturbance types across local (500 km2) to continental (6.5 x 10^6 km2) extents; insect damage studies at local extents as low as about 23%
notes: DECISIVE RECORD FOR THE RQ3 ADJUDICATION. Stahl et al. 2023, full text read. This is a complete synthesis of the automated attribution literature to April 2022. Three findings bear directly on the novelty claim. First, all biotic agents collapse into a single attribution category, described verbatim as 'biotic disturbances or other stress, referring to degradation of the forest canopy due to insect damage, disease, or unspecified stress (which can include abiotic or anthropogenic drivers such as drought or acidification)', so no reviewed study separated one insect from another. Second, the words lidar and LiDAR do not appear anywhere in the paper. Third, radar appears once, prospectively: 'The addition of Sentinel data (including Sentinel-1 radar data) to attribution algorithms may help foster additional advances in research and monitoring of forest disturbance and recovery... potentially providing greater sensitivity for earlier detection of tree stress.' Absent from references.bib.

title: Estimation of leaf loss rate in pest damaged larch forests using Sentinel-2 satellite data
venue: Mongolian Journal of Geography and Geoecology
method: spectral index and spectral derivative features from simulated and non-simulated Sentinel-2A reflectance, SPA feature selection, random forest discrimination model of pest type, FCM clustering for severity
sensor: Sentinel-2A, plus ground spectroscopy for the simulation model
agent: Erannis jacobsoni Djak and Dendrolimus sibiricus Tschtv, two insect defoliators
support: tree and plot within two study areas
validation_design: cross-validated (mR2cv, rR2cv reported), no spatial blocking stated
accuracy_metric: cross-validated R squared and RMSE for leaf loss rate by pest and feature set
accuracy_value: simulated Sentinel-2A: EJD spectral index mR2cv 0.8771, PST spectral index mR2cv 0.8900; non-simulated: EJD 0.7907, PST 0.8094
notes: NEAREST MISS FOR THE TWO-INSECT CLAIM, full text read. Ariunaa et al. 2022. It does build a random forest discrimination model of different pest types, and both agents are defoliators of larch. But the two agents occupy two separate study areas, Binder for Erannis jacobsoni and Baruunburen for Dendrolimus sibiricus, several hundred kilometres apart, so agent is fully confounded with site, climate and stand. The paper reports leaf loss rate accuracy per pest, not a confusion matrix between the two pests. It therefore does not refute a claim about separating two insect agents attacking the same host in the same place.

title: Changes in Spatiotemporal Pattern and Its Driving Factors of Suburban Forest Defoliating Pest Disasters
method: leaf area index time series from Sentinel-2A across a full 3 to 5 year disaster cycle, with geographical detector analysis of driving factors
host: forest of the Changbai Mountain region, multiple forest types
notes: Covers a complete outbreak cycle rather than a single epoch, and separates driver contributions by growth stage.

title: Early Detection of Dendroctonus valens Infestation at Tree Level with a Hyperspectral UAV Image
method: random forest and convolutional neural network on reflectance, derivatives and spectral vegetation indices, three tree states
accuracy_value: dead trees separated accurately by all models; infested-tree change confined mainly to the visible region
notes: Dead trees are easy and infested trees are hard, the same asymmetry that governs whether the adelgid class is detectable at all.

title: Uncovering Early Traces of Bark Beetle Induced Forest Stress via Semantically Enriched Sentinel-2 Data and Spectral Indices
venue: PFG – Journal of Photogrammetry Remote Sensing and Geoinformation Science
method: stratified hierarchical hybrid image understanding system pre-selecting candidate pixels, then spectral vegetation indices to confirm or reject
notes: States the general contrast that matters here: unlike sudden agents such as wind, avalanche and fire, bark beetle infestation progresses gradually. The same gradualness applies to adelgid damage.

title: Detecting semi-arid forest decline using time series of Landsat data
method: three Landsat time series approaches compared, random forest, anomaly detection and Sen's slope
accuracy_value: random forest 0.75 (kappa 0.50), anomaly detection 0.65 (kappa 0.30), Sen's slope 0.64 (kappa 0.30)
notes: Sparse open canopies again, and a candid set of low kappa values for a two-class decline problem.

title: Monitoring and Prediction of Siberian Silk Moth Dendrolimus sibiricus Tschetv. (Lepidoptera: Lasiocampidae) Outbreaks Using Remote Sensing Techniques
method: construction of remote indicators based on stand response to weather conditions, aimed at detecting loss of resistance before damage appears
sensor: satellite remote sensing, sensors not enumerated in abstract
notes: States plainly that many remote indicators only change after significant damage has occurred, which is the timing problem in matching a survey polygon to imagery.

title: Exploring the potential to use in-between pixel variability for early detection of bark beetle attacked trees
method: coefficient of variation of four vegetation indices computed in 3x3, 4x4 and 5x5 pixel windows through a time series
notes: Uses within-neighbourhood spectral variability rather than mean reflectance, a texture route to a subtle signal.

title: A Sentinel-2 Based Multi-Temporal Monitoring Framework for Wind and Bark Beetle Detection and Damage Mapping
method: multi-temporal Sentinel-2 time series framework for detecting and mapping both windthrow and subsequent bark beetle damage
host: coniferous forest, Friulian Dolomites, Carnic and Julian Alps
notes: Sets out to distinguish the cause of forest damage between an abiotic and a biotic agent that are causally linked, the wind-then-beetle cascade.

title: Agents of Forest Disturbance in the Argentine Dry Chaco
method: random forest classification of disturbance patches on spectral characteristics and patch shape metrics
agent: logging, fire, partial clearing, riparian change and drought
host: Argentine Dry Chaco dry forest, 489,000 km2
accuracy_value: partial clearing was the most widespread type
notes: Five-class attribution using patch shape as well as spectra. The classes differ in geometry, which is what makes shape metrics work.

title: Characterization of Wildfires and Harvesting Forest Disturbances and Recovery Using Landsat Time Series: A Case Study in Mediterranean Forests in Central Italy
method: pixel-level spectral trajectory extraction over 20 years with short and long-term recovery metrics, by disturbance type
notes: Separates two agents by their distinct pre and post-event temporal behaviour, which is the mechanism this project cannot rely on because both its agents are chronic.

title: Distinguishing Abrupt and Gradual Forest Disturbances With MODIS-Based Phenological Anomaly Series
method: phenological anomaly series from MODIS to distinguish abrupt from gradual disturbance
agent: abrupt versus gradual disturbance, agents not individually named
host: forest, extent not stated in abstract
notes: Splits disturbance by temporal form rather than by agent, which is the axis on which most optical attribution actually operates.

title: Mapping Cork Oak Mortality Using Multitemporal High-Resolution Satellite Imagery
method: change detection with an unsupervised classifier on three vegetation indices between dates
host: cork oak (Quercus suber) in a pasture with multiple species
notes: Open pasture-woodland with mixed species, the hardest optical background, addressed at individual tree support.

title: Storm and fire disturbances in Europe: Distribution and trends
method: random forest classifier assigning 27 million satellite-mapped disturbance patches to storm or fire, using a large reference dataset of true occurrences
agent: storm and fire, against a background of biotic and human agents
validation_design: large reference dataset of true disturbance occurrences
notes: The largest patch-level agent classification in the set by sample size. Its two positive classes are both abiotic and everything else is residual.

title: Early detection of bark beetle infestation in Norway spruce forests of Central Europe using Sentinel-2
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: seasonal trajectories of Sentinel-2 bands and vegetation indices tested for green-attack detection at stand rather than tree level
agent: Ips spp. bark beetle green attack
support: forest stand, explicitly not individual tree
notes: States explicitly that Sentinel-2 does not allow individual tree detection, which fixes the support at which a Sentinel-based design can operate.

title: Extending deep learning approaches for forest disturbance segmentation on very high‐resolution satellite images
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
method: deep convolutional neural networks for segmentation of damage on very high resolution imagery
notes: Recognises damage from two agents, one abiotic and one biotic, in a single segmentation framework.

title: Detecting subtle change from dense Landsat time series: Case studies of mountain pine beetle and spruce beetle disturbance
method: dense Landsat time series change detection applied to two insect case studies
agent: mountain pine beetle and spruce beetle
host: lodgepole pine and Engelmann spruce respectively
notes: Identity resolved by title only. No abstract was retrievable from Semantic Scholar or Crossref and the full text was not opened, so nothing about its method or results is asserted here. Flagged as a priority full-text read: it is the only record in the set whose title names two insect agents in one study, although the two agents attack different hosts.

title: Disturbance detection in landsat time series is influenced by tree mortality agent and severity, not by prior disturbance
method: comparison of LandTrendr products against a field dataset and against alternative mapping methods, on a landscape with both wildfire and spruce beetle
host: spruce forest, landscape disturbed since about 2000
validation_design: unique field dataset from a landscape with a known history of both agents
accuracy_metric: relative detectability by agent and severity, and area predicted
accuracy_value: LandTrendr more accurately detected wildfire than spruce beetle-induced mortality; both were more easily detected at high severity; LandTrendr predicted about 40% lower affected area than alternative approaches
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR OMISSION BIAS. Demonstrates that detection probability itself depends on which agent caused the mortality, so an attribution model trained on optically detected disturbance inherits an agent-dependent sampling bias. Also finds that prior spruce beetle outbreaks did not influence detectability of subsequent wildfire.

title: Human or natural? Landscape context improves the attribution of forest disturbances mapped from Landsat in Central Europe
method: causal attribution using a novel indicator class characterising landscape context, applied to 1.01 million disturbance patches
validation_design: reference data on 2620 patches from targeted field observations and structured interviews with 21 forest managers
notes: Already cited as Sebald 2021. Its reference-data protocol, field observation plus manager interview on 2620 patches, is the most careful in the set. Its key predictor is landscape context, which is site information rather than damage signature.

title: Detection of Bark Beetle Disturbance at Tree Level Using UAS Multispectral Imagery and Deep Learning
method: three CNN architectures and random forest classifying four categories including green attack, from UAS multispectral
sensor: UAS multispectral, RGB bands sufficient for the best models
agent: bark beetle, green attack and later stages
accuracy_value: best kappa 0.80 (Nez4c3b CNN) and 0.76 (Safaugu4c3b CNN) using RGB bands only
notes: States verbatim that the main misclassifications were between the two infestation stages because of the similar spectral responses, and that merging them made the model type less important. A direct warning about class definition.

title: Forest disturbances and the attribution derived from yearly Landsat time series over 1990–2020 in the Hengduan Mountains Region of Southwest China
method: LandTrendr on Google Earth Engine for detection, then random forest attribution using disturbance properties with spectral and topographic variables
agent: fire, logging, road construction and insects
host: Hengduan Mountains natural forest, southwest China
accuracy_value: disturbance map 92.3% conventional and 97.70% +/- 0.06% area-adjusted; agent attribution 85.80%
notes: Four-agent attribution including an insect class, at 85.80% overall. Insects are a single undivided class and topography contributes to the discrimination.

title: Mapping European Spruce Bark Beetle Infestation at Its Early Phase Using Gyrocopter-Mounted Hyperspectral Data and Field Measurements
method: new hyperspectral index defined from 0.3 m airborne data, compared with common indices and validated against field spectrometry and a second study area
sensor: gyrocopter-mounted hyperspectral at 0.3 m, field spectrometer
validation_design: field data validation plus long-term validation in a second study area for transferability
notes: Highest reported accuracy for green attack in the set, at 0.3 m from an airborne platform with an independent transferability test. Sets the practical ceiling that satellite-scale work is measured against.

title: Detection of drought‐induced blue oak mortality in the Sierra Nevada Mountains, California
method: identification of the most predictive wavelength regions from airborne hyperspectral, then mapping
host: blue oak (Quercus douglasii) woodland, Sierra Nevada foothills
accuracy_value: a normalized ratio of 937.53 and 1100.08 nm correlated with mortality at R2 0.83
notes: Open savanna-like woodland, and the stated difficulty is discriminating dead from live in arid deciduous canopies.

title: Early detection of a tree pathogen using airborne remote sensing.
method: repeat laser-guided imaging spectroscopy in two years, mapping foliar trait indices distinguishing infected from healthy trees
sensor: Global Airborne Observatory laser-guided imaging spectroscopy, 2018 and 2019
validation_design: repeat acquisition, further design not stated in abstract
notes: Laser-guided spectroscopy, so structure informs the spectral retrieval, for early detection of a pathogen on one host.

title: Sentinel-2 Data in an Evaluation of the Impact of the Disturbances on Forest Vegetation
method: time series analysis of vegetation and tasseled cap indices across five areas of contrasting degradation type, validated with in situ data and aerial photographs
agent: bark beetle calamity, plus recovery and undisturbed controls
host: Low Tatras and Sumava National Parks, spruce
validation_design: in situ data and aerial photographs across five contrasting case areas
class_balance_reported: yes, five areas by degradation type stated
notes: Includes undisturbed control areas as well as disturbed ones, which most detection studies omit.

title: Tree Species Classification and Health Status Assessment for a Mixed Broadleaf-Conifer Forest with UAS Multispectral Imaging
method: two-step classification, first broadleaf versus conifer, then health status within tree type, from bi-temporal 5-band UAS imagery with structure from motion
sensor: UAS 5-band multispectral with structure-from-motion terrain models
notes: Classifies host type first and health second, the same ordering this project needs in order to hold host constant.

title: Change in forest condition: Characterizing non-stand replacing disturbances using time series satellite imagery
method: time series satellite imagery characterising non-stand-replacing disturbances by extent, severity and persistence
sensor: time series satellite imagery, Landsat family
agent: drought stress and insect infestation as non-stand-replacing agents
host: forest, extent not stated in abstract
notes: Names the non-stand-replacing class as the underserved case and attributes the neglect to subtle alterations to forest canopies and structure. The adelgid signal in British Columbia is in this class.

title: Image Processing Techniques based Feature Extraction for Insect Damage Areas
method: grey-level co-occurrence matrix texture feature extraction for segmenting damaged from healthy areas
notes: Texture rather than spectral mean as the discriminating feature.

title: Determining the Drying Out of Coniferous Trees Using Airborne and Satellite Data
method: linear discriminant analysis supervised classification of satellite imagery calibrated against airborne photo-spectral measurements
sensor: TripleSat multispectral, airborne spectrometers 400 to 900 nm
agent: bark beetle causing conifer drying out
validation_design: airborne measurements as reference for satellite classification
accuracy_value: 27% to 74% for the airborne data across drying-out stages
notes: Honest reporting of very low accuracy at early stages, which most studies do not show.

title: Automatic Tree Crown Feature Extraction from UAS Multispectral Imagery for the Detection of Bark Beetle Disturbance in an Urban Forest
method: individual tree crown delineation followed by crown feature extraction
notes: Conference abstract. Notes that urban stressors change the baseline against which infestation is detected.

title: Threshold- and trend-based vegetation change monitoring algorithm based on the inter-annual multi-temporal normalized difference moisture index series: A case study of the Tatra Mountains
method: threshold- and trend-based vegetation change monitoring algorithm on an inter-annual normalized difference moisture index series
sensor: Landsat TM, ETM+ and OLI, 51 images 1984 to 2016
agent: strong winds and bark beetle outbreaks
notes: Designed to catch gradual as well as abrupt change, which most algorithms cannot.

title: Automatic Tree Crown Extraction from UAS Multispectral Imagery for the Detection of Bark Beetle Disturbance in Mixed Forests
method: excess green index masking to isolate conifers, then individual tree crown delineation and crown feature extraction
sensor: UAS multispectral orthomosaic, photogrammetric point cloud
host: mixed urban forest, conifers among deciduous
notes: Uses a spectral mask to isolate the host before detecting the agent, and uses a photogrammetric point cloud rather than lidar for the structural component.

title: Mapping Multiple Insect Outbreaks across Large Regions Annually Using Landsat Time Series Data
method: tree-level mortality maps from high-resolution imagery used as reference to train Landsat classification and random forest percent-mortality regression, applied on Google Earth Engine
sensor: high-resolution multispectral imagery, Landsat time series 1984 to 2018
agent: insect-caused tree mortality, a variety of agents
host: three coniferous forests, western United States
validation_design: cross-validated random forest, high-resolution reference imagery from three years
accuracy_metric: overall accuracy for disturbed versus undisturbed, and variance explained for percent mortality
accuracy_value: 74% to 80% overall accuracy for disturbed versus undisturbed; cross-validated random forest explained 61% to 68% of variation in percent mortality within disturbed 30 m pixels
notes: Already cited as Bright 2020. Its comparison against vector aerial survey data is directly relevant to RQ4, and the abstract records that low-level tree mortality was not always detected.

title: Continuous Detection of Small-Scale Changes in Scots Pine Dominated Stands Using Dense Sentinel-2 Time Series
method: continuous change detection on a dense Sentinel-2 time series, 49 images
agent: drought and disturbance in pine and spruce stands
notes: Aimed at small-scale change, the size class most aerial survey polygons fall into.

title: A satellite-derived database for stand-replacing windthrow events in boreal forests of European Russia in 1986–2017
method: delineation from the full Landsat archive plus two forest change products, then manual verification of each event to assign storm type and date
agent: windthrow from convective and non-convective storms
support: damage patch, 102,747 elementary areas in 700 events
accuracy_value: 102,747 damaged areas combined into 700 windthrow events caused by 486 storms
notes: Rare case where every mapped event was manually verified and attributed to a named meteorological cause.

title: Forest Disturbances in Polish Tatra Mountains for 1985–2016 in Relation to Topography, Stand Features, and Protection Zone
method: analysis of disturbance frequency against topography, stand features and protection zone
agent: windthrow, snow avalanche and bark beetle outbreak
notes: Quantifies how much of the disturbance pattern is explained by elevation, aspect, slope and stand age, which is the site confound in agent attribution.

title: An Examination of an Enhanced Remote Sensing Method for Agent Attribution of Forest Disturbance
method: random forest attribution of three agents from Landsat temporal segmentation, patch geometry and grey-level co-occurrence matrix texture metrics, with and without texture
accuracy_value: 72.0% texture-free and 72.2% texture-dependent, with no significant difference between them
notes: A clean negative result: adding landscape texture metrics did not improve agent attribution. Worth citing before adding texture predictors here. The abstract also notes that harvest concentrated at mid-elevations and fire and stress at lower elevations, again showing elevation carrying the discrimination.

title: Detection of Fir Trees (Abies sibirica) Damaged by the Bark Beetle in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Images with Deep Learning
method: two-stage deep learning, region proposal then crown classification by damage stage
notes: Fir host with a bark beetle agent, and states that trees at different damage stages coexist and overlap in the canopy, which is the mixed-severity polygon problem.

title: The Use of UAV Mounted Sensors for Precise Detection of Bark Beetle Infestation
method: evaluation of UAV-mounted low-cost sensors in an unmanaged zone where infested trees are not removed
host: Norway spruce, Krkonose Mountains National Park
validation_design: unmanaged zone allowing continuous monitoring of infested trees that are not salvaged
notes: Rare design in which salvage logging does not remove the signal before it can be observed.

title: Timing of red-edge and shortwave infrared reflectance critical for early stress detection induced by bark beetle (Ips typographus, L.) attack
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
method: temporal analysis of leaf traits and reflectance from high-resolution satellite time series with field data through the attack sequence
accuracy_value: red-edge and shortwave infrared timing identified as critical
notes: Identifies which spectral regions carry the early signal and when, which constrains the imagery epoch a design can use.

title: A comprehensive evaluation of disturbance agent classification approaches: Strengths of ensemble classification, multiple indices, spatio-temporal variables, and direct prediction
method: six approaches compared, two-stage and direct prediction of agent from trajectory-based temporal segmentation of five spectral indices, with and without spatio-temporal variables
agent: disturbance agents, classes not enumerated in abstract
host: forest, region not stated in abstract
validation_design: comparative accuracy evaluation across six approaches
accuracy_value: 92.4% for direct prediction with spatio-temporal variables, significantly higher than 90.9% for two-stage prediction
notes: The most careful published comparison of attribution architectures. Finds that spatial variables help pixel-based direct prediction but are redundant in patch-based two-stage prediction because the patch already carries the spatial information.

title: Estimating the Threshold of Detection on Tree Crown Defoliation Using Vegetation Indices from UAS Multispectral Imagery
method: nested histogram thresholding on four UAS vegetation indices to detect defoliation and distinguish pine species, offered as an alternative to random forest
validation_design: four study areas, classification accuracy evaluated
accuracy_metric: classification accuracy and a detection threshold on defoliation
accuracy_value: NDVI and NDVI red edge performed best; threshold value not extracted from abstract
notes: Explicitly estimates the defoliation level below which detection fails, which is the quantity a severity-limited design most needs.

title: Object-Based Classification of Forest Disturbance Types in the Conterminous United States
method: segmentation of forest cover loss into objects then random forest attribution trained on expert-interpreted high-resolution imagery, applied to all 15,179,430 loss objects
sensor: Landsat-based Global Forest Change product and Web-Enabled Landsat Data, 2003 to 2011
validation_design: independent dataset of 4156 forest loss objects
accuracy_metric: overall accuracy, omission and commission error by class
accuracy_value: overall accuracy 88.1%; highest omission error for fire at 32.8% and highest commission error for stress at 31.9%; 83.75% of loss attributed to stem removal, 10.92% fire, 5.33% stress
notes: Only high-magnitude loss over 50% cover is attributed, and all biotic and abiotic decline collapses into a single 'stress' class with the worst commission error of the three.

title: Climate-Triggered Insect Defoliators and Forest Fires Using Multitemporal Landsat and TerraClimate Data in NE Iran: An Application of GEOBIA TreeNet and Panel Data Analysis
method: object-based image analysis with TreeNet boosted trees, then panel data models linking defoliation intensity to fire severity under climate variables
host: broadleaved mixed Hyrcanian forest, northeast Iran
notes: Two agents present, but the second agent is modelled as a consequence of the first rather than as a competing explanation.

title: Accuracy of aerial detection surveys for mapping insect and disease disturbances in the United States
method: error matrices comparing aerial detection survey observations against ground-collected data, in a stepdown from broad categories to specific damage agents, plus a repeatability test among surveyors
sensor: operational aerial detection survey (sketch mapping) against ground observation
agent: insects, diseases and abiotic events, from feeding guild down to species
host: United States forest across multiple ecological regions
support: survey polygon, with a small-polygon subset analysed separately
validation_design: independent ground observation, error matrices, plus repeated observation by different surveyors
accuracy_metric: overall accuracy, commission error by category
accuracy_value: overall accuracy above 70% in all error matrices; commission error 2% for tree mortality and 5% for defoliation as damage types; 9% commission error for bark beetle-caused mortality; accuracy declined as specificity went from genus to species for both tree species and damaging agent
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ4, already cited as Coleman 2018. The finding that accuracy declines from genus to species level is the direct constraint on this project, because balsam woolly adelgid and western balsam bark beetle are both species-level attributions on the same host genus.

title: Confirmation of post-harvest spectral recovery from Landsat time series using measures of forest cover and height derived from airborne laser scanning data
method: spectral years-to-recovery metric from Landsat compared against ALS-derived cover and height in regenerating stands
sensor: Landsat time series, airborne laser scanning
validation_design: ALS structure as independent corroboration of a spectral metric
notes: Exactly the cross-check this project needs in reverse: it uses structure to verify what a spectral index claims, rather than using structure as the predictor.

title: Natural disturbances are spatially diverse but temporally synchronized across temperate forest landscapes in Europe
method: landscape analysis of Landsat-based disturbance maps across five unmanaged forest landscapes, testing topographic and climatic drivers
agent: natural disturbance, agents not individually named
host: temperate European forest, five unmanaged landscapes
notes: Finds disturbance spatially diverse but temporally synchronised, which is why survey year is a confound rather than a neutral covariate.

title: Landsat Imagery Spectral Trajectories - Important Variables for Spatially Predicting the Risks of Bark Beetle Disturbance
method: pre-disturbance Landsat spectral trajectories introduced as a long-term stress indicator into infestation risk models with environmental predictors
sensor: Landsat Thematic Mapper, aerial photographs 1991 and 1994 to 2000 as reference
host: Sumava Mountains spruce, Czech and German border
validation_design: annual aerial photograph delineations as reference
notes: Uses the history of a pixel before the disturbance as a predictor, which is available here because the aerial overview survey archive is long.

title: Differentiation of Alternate Harvesting Practices Using Annual Time Series of Landsat Data
method: annual Landsat time series with spectral metrics and attributed change products to distinguish harvest prescriptions by canopy cover removed
agent: clearcut, clearcut with residual, partial and selective cutting
notes: Separates classes that differ only in severity within one agent, which is closer to the adelgid-versus-beetle problem than most wind-versus-beetle work, though the agent is human and the timing is instantaneous.

title: Satellite-based hyperspectral imaging and cartographic visualization of bark beetle forest damage for the city of Čabar
method: semi-automatic classification of satellite hyperspectral imagery to map bark beetle spread following ice damage
agent: ice rain damage followed by bark beetle spread
host: forest of the city of Cabar, Croatia
notes: Short paper. Another instance of an abiotic event followed by a biotic agent on the same stands.

title: Classification of Airborne Multispectral Scanner Data for Mapping Current Defoliation Caused by the Spruce Budworm
method: classification of airborne multispectral scanner bands, ratios, differences and principal components into three current-defoliation levels
accuracy_value: three levels of current defoliation classified (heavy, light, healthy); little advantage beyond four bands
notes: 1988. States that cumulative defoliation and mixed-wood areas caused confusions in the classifications, which is the same confusion this project faces between chronic adelgid damage and mixed stand composition.

title: Application of CNN and Vision Transformer Models for Classifying Crowns in Pine Plantations Affected by Diplodia Shoot Blight
method: convolutional neural network and vision transformer models detecting and classifying infected crowns across five sites and two acquisition years
validation_design: five geographically dispersed sites with varying topography, two years
notes: States explicitly that aerial sketch-mapping and manual photo interpretation for tree health surveys are labour-intensive and subjective, and offers deep learning as the replacement.

title: Historical insect disturbance maps from 1985 onwards for Canadian forests derived using earth observation data
method: Landsat-based annual mapping of severe insect defoliation, evaluated against aerial survey classes
agent: boreal forest insect pests causing severe canopy loss
validation_design: evaluated against aggregated moderate and severe pest classes
accuracy_value: 90% between the aggregated moderate-and-severe pest class and the non-pest class
notes: CENTRAL FOR RQ4 AND FOR CANADA. States that current monitoring relies on costly and subjective aerial survey interpretations, and that no consistent long-term satellite dataset previously existed for severe canopy loss in coniferous forests. Its 90% figure applies only to a two-class aggregation, not to agent identity.

title: Sentinel-2-Based Forest Health Survey of ICP Forests Level I and II Plots in Hungary
method: standardised NDVI anomaly maps compared against ground-based ICP Forests plot assessments
host: Hungarian forest, 7 Level II and 78 Level I plots
validation_design: agreement between satellite damage categories and ground plot assessments
accuracy_metric: agreement between satellite and ground damage classes
accuracy_value: agreement reported between Level II plots and the five severity categories, figures not extracted from abstract
notes: Ground plot network as the reference for a satellite damage classification, the same validation structure this project needs.

title: Spatially explicit forest mortality forecasts are driven by autocorrelation, not ecological context
method: gradient-boosted regression compared against naive autocorrelation models at continental and local scale, with an assessment of bias and variability among aerial survey observers
sensor: aerial detection surveys, satellite imagery change, high-resolution individual dead tree mapping
support: survey polygon, pixel and individual tree
validation_design: comparison of models trained on different mortality data sources, plus an observer bias assessment
notes: CENTRAL FOR RQ4. Preprint. Directly evaluates bias and variability among aerial survey observers, and reports that spatially explicit mortality forecasts are driven by autocorrelation rather than by ecological context, which is a warning about spatially unblocked validation.

title: Precision Detection and Assessment of Ash Death and Decline Caused by the Emerald Ash Borer Using Drones and Deep Learning
method: deep learning model trained on 6174 drone aerial images of ash decline
host: Fraxinus spp., West Virginia and Pennsylvania
notes: States that visual ground and aerial surveys are generally effective but inefficient for precisely locating declining trees in large or hard-to-access areas.

title: Wall-to-wall mapping of carbon loss within the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone after the 2020 catastrophic wildfire
method: radar backscatter delta before and after fire, and a radar-based change model, predicting carbon loss from stand-wise inventory and local combustion factors
host: planted forest of the Chornobyl Exclusion Zone
validation_design: stand-wise inventory data where field observation is impossible
accuracy_value: both the standalone Sentinel-1 backscatter delta and the radar-based change model reliably predicted carbon loss
notes: Radar carries a damage magnitude where no field access is possible, which is the operational argument for radar in inaccessible coastal British Columbia.

title: Detecting Pest-Infested Forest Damage through Multispectral Satellite Imagery and Improved UNet++
method: UNet++ with an attention module, combining multispectral bands, vegetation indices and RGB
host: forest, region not stated in abstract
notes: Tests whether adding non-visible bands and indices to RGB improves segmentation of pest damage.

title: Detecting White Pine Needle Damage through Satellite Remote Sensing
method: random forest feature selection then binary and severity classification from Sentinel-2 spectral vegetation indices
agent: White Pine Needle Damage, a fungal disease complex
validation_design: aerial detection survey outbreak records as reference
accuracy_metric: binary detection accuracy and severity classification accuracy
accuracy_value: 70% for binary WPND versus non-WPND detection; severity accuracy not extracted from abstract
notes: Explicitly positioned as complementing field and aerial detection surveys rather than replacing them. 70% is a realistic figure for a subtle needle-damage signal at Sentinel-2 support.

title: Accuracy of Defoliation Estimates from Aerial and Ground Surveys in a Boreal Forest during an Outbreak of the Hemlock Looper, Lambdina fiscellaria (Guenée)
method: aerial survey defoliation classes compared with ground-based Fettes-method estimates on current-year and four preceding years of foliage
sensor: operational aerial survey against ground estimation
validation_design: paired aerial and ground estimates through an outbreak
accuracy_metric: accuracy of aerial defoliation classes against ground estimates
accuracy_value: accurate for light and moderate defoliation in the first outbreak year; lower accuracy at both ends of the defoliation gradient and much less reliable after the first year
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ4. Shows that aerial survey severity accuracy is not stable across the outbreak, and that it degrades exactly where the gradient is extreme. Directly relevant to why severity was excluded as a response in this project.

title: Using Satellite Imagery to Evaluate Bark Beetle-Caused Tree Mortality Reported in Aerial Surveys in a Mixed Conifer Forest in Northern Idaho, USA
method: beetle-caused mortality mapped from two WorldView-2 images, then used to evaluate Insect and Disease Survey severity estimates
sensor: WorldView-2 fine-resolution satellite imagery against operational aerial survey
validation_design: independent satellite-derived mortality used as reference for survey polygons
accuracy_metric: agreement between survey severity estimates and satellite-derived mortality
notes: CENTRAL RECORD FOR RQ4.
